authorities.locator: Section 1291, preliminary edition current through July 29, 2026
authorities.proposition: The courts of appeals have jurisdiction over appeals from final decisions of the district courts, subject to statutory exceptions not implicated by the final judgment in this synthetic FOIA action.

authorities.locator: Section 552(a)(8)(A), (b)(7)(E)-(F), and the reasonably-segregable sentence following subsection (b)(9), preliminary edition current through July 29, 2026
authorities.proposition: FOIA permits withholding law-enforcement records to the extent production would disclose investigation or prosecution techniques and procedures, or guidelines whose disclosure could reasonably be expected to risk circumvention of law, and to the extent production could reasonably be expected to endanger an individual's life or physical safety. An agency also must disclose reasonably segregable nonexempt portions and ordinarily may withhold only when it reasonably foresees harm to an interest protected by an exemption or disclosure is prohibited by law.

authorities.locator: Local Rule 105.11, official Local Rules pages 18-19
authorities.proposition: A sealing motion must identify the material, state why sealing is necessary, explain why alternatives will not protect the interest at stake, and propose a duration. The motion remains publicly docketed for at least fourteen days before disposition, and an unsupported failure to justify sealing permits denial.

Training and operational records can satisfy Exemption 7's law-enforcement-purpose threshold. Exemption 7(E) protects nonpublic implementation details of law-enforcement techniques or procedures even when the general technique is publicly known; the statutory risk-of-circumvention qualifier modifies guidelines, not techniques and procedures.

authorities.citation: Rein v. U.S. Patent & Trademark Office, 553 F.3d 353 (4th Cir. 2009)
authorities.locator: No. 07-1738, official slip opinion pages 19-26 and 33-36
authorities.proposition: An agency must describe withheld material and the claimed exemption with enough specificity to permit adversarial testing and meaningful de novo review. The agency also bears the segregability burden and must show that it disclosed all reasonably segregable nonexempt information rather than rely on a conclusory declaration.

authorities.citation: Zaid v. U.S. Department of Justice, 96 F.4th 697 (4th Cir. 2024)
authorities.proposition: FOIA exemption rulings receive de novo review, and the agency bears the burden of proving withheld material fits an exemption on an adequate factual basis. A categorical presentation remains permissible only when founded on document-by-document review and meaningful functional categories tied to the protected interest and the asserted disclosure harm.

authorities.citation: Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility v. U.S. Section, International Boundary & Water Commission, 740 F.3d 195 (D.C. Cir. 2014)
authorities.proposition: Emergency-response records for critical infrastructure may be compiled for a law-enforcement purpose when they address prevention of and response to criminal threats. Exemptions 7(E) and 7(F) still require a concrete explanation linking disclosure of the particular operational information to circumvention or a reasonable threat to physical safety.

authorities.citation: Electronic Privacy Information Center v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security, 777 F.3d 518 (D.C. Cir. 2015)
authorities.locator: No. 14-5013, official slip opinion pages 1 and 8-16
authorities.proposition: Exemption 7(F) does not require an agency to identify threatened people by name, but the agency must demonstrate that disclosure could reasonably be expected to endanger some individual's life or physical safety. A valid 7(F) showing does not dispense with a distinct, supported segregability determination.

authorities.citation: Company Doe v. Public Citizen, 749 F.3d 246 (4th Cir. 2014)
authorities.proposition: Before sealing judicial records, a court must identify the governing source of public access, give public notice and an opportunity to object, consider less drastic alternatives, and make specific findings supporting closure. First Amendment sealing additionally demands a compelling interest and narrow tailoring, so an entire case or broad group of filings cannot be sealed merely because portions contain sensitive information.
